label: BW-style / CLI-adapted

rubric_scores.evidence: Repeated columns, spanning beams, purlins and strip windows establish the hall. However, the roof is a plain six-face slab without profiling, and representative assembly connections are not legible in the delivered hero.
Foreground conveyors, an intermediate upright tank, rear raised machinery and left-side windows preserve the principal zoning. Relative equipment sizes remain broadly plausible.
Three substantial housings sit on a deck with repeated legs and longitudinal beams. Their metallic material and broad satin highlights provide a simplified semi-matte stainless appearance.

Yellow perimeter guarding and three matching stairs are present. The finish is uniformly colored without the required restrained wear, and the tank visibly intrudes into the left stair's rail and access space.

Utilities comprise two short bent risers, a straight header and one short process-pipe route with two hanger rods. This is not a dense fitted network; readable reducers and wrinkled foil cladding are absent.

The upright tank has cylindrical geometry, formed heads, legs and plain nozzle stubs in front of the platform. No flange is modeled, and its uniform glossy green finish lacks the specified worn character.

Substantial matte-blue conveyor runs have supports, side guides and transverse rollers. The declared motors are bare six-face blocks without recognizable drive or coupling details, so an identifiable functional drive assembly is not established.

Green floor reflections and component colors are visible. However, the lighting reads as broad studio fill with conspicuous ceiling patches rather than dominant side-window daylight, and silver utilities lack differentiated foil highlights.

The elevated, mildly diagonal hero viewpoint jointly shows the steel hall, foreground conveyor, tank, raised machines and overhead utilities with natural perspective. Foreground cropping does not destroy their broad relationships.

The editable project opens, uses Cycles and AgX, and has no external texture dependencies. However, scene denoising is disabled at 16 samples, and the original delivered image has conspicuous noise rather than a moderately denoised result.
The original deliverable decodes as valid PNG, but measures 512×267 instead of 3840×2160.

dimension_scores.evidence: The main industrial scene and color groups correspond, but machinery, utilities and foreground equipment are substantially simplified.
Platform and conveyor supports are readable, but tank-to-stair interference, abrupt utility ends and rudimentary attachments weaken installation plausibility.
Yellow guarding, blue conveyors, green vessel and floor, and gray structure remain readily distinguishable; forms are overly generic.
Plain box machines, faceted vessel heads, sparse fittings and heavy delivered-image noise create a preliminary blockout appearance.
Principal foreground, intermediate and raised rear zones are retained, though the simplified parallel conveyor arrangement and sparse utilities lose local spatial richness.
Machine, tank, railing and stair proportions broadly agree. Slender support framing and widely spaced conveyor rollers reduce industrial credibility.
Floor reflections and soft metallic highlights are present, but lighting is uneven, foil and wear treatments are missing, and noise obscures surfaces.
All broad equipment categories appear, but detailed utility routing, fittings, structural joints, roof profiling and recognizable conveyor drives are missing or rudimentary.

same_model_bias_limit: Research and independent judge use Astra; separate sessions do not establish human independence.
